purpose: Per CEO R299 P0+P1: 'Do not kill P-15. Build Power Architecture Tree (A/B/C/D/E). Source every energy number with provenance state.'
constitutional_basis: Article XXVII (every threshold has provenance). Article XXV (unknown must remain unknown). Article XXIX (separate implementation failure from mechanism failure — 'this architecture failed' ≠ 'the concept is dead').

energy_number_provenance_system.rule: No number appears without a provenance state. 'Typical' without a source is forbidden.
energy_number_provenance_system.anti_inflation: MODELLED numbers cannot be used to kill a candidate. Only LITERATURE_VERIFIED or EXPERIMENTALLY_MEASURED can support a kill decision.

cardiac_harvesting.description: Piezoelectric generator producing 15 μA in vivo, directly powering a cardiac pacemaker demonstration
cardiac_harvesting.power_estimate_uW: ~150 μW (at 10V pacing output, 15 μA = 150 μW instantaneous during pacing pulse)
cardiac_harvesting.notes: This is INSTANTANEOUS power during a pacing pulse, not continuous. Duty cycle matters.

cardiac_harvesting.value: 100 μF capacitor charged to 4V in 13 minutes
cardiac_harvesting.description: Piezoelectric system implanted on pig heart, charged capacitor and operated commercial pacemaker
cardiac_harvesting.power_estimate_uW: Energy = 0.5 × 100e-6 × 4² = 0.8 mJ. Over 780 seconds = ~1.03 μW average charging power
cardiac_harvesting.notes: Average power ~1 μW to charge capacitor. But this charged enough to OPERATE a pacemaker — meaning the pacemaker's duty cycle is compatible with this harvesting rate.

cardiac_harvesting.description: Comprehensive review of piezoelectric energy harvesting for pacemaker applications
cardiac_harvesting.power_estimate_uW: Range: 0.1-100 μW depending on design, size, and coupling
cardiac_harvesting.notes: Review covers state-of-the-art. Best designs approach 100 μW. Typical is lower.

cardiac_harvesting.description: Experimental study on piezoelectric vibration energy harvester for self-powered cardiac pacemakers
cardiac_harvesting.power_estimate_uW: Not specified in abstract — need full paper
cardiac_harvesting.notes: Additional evidence that cardiac harvesting is an active field with experimental validation

csf_harvesting.description: Energy harvesting from CSF pressure fluctuations. 2.5mm piezoelectric harvester. 0.62 nW max measured.
csf_harvesting.notes: This is MEASURED, not modelled. Extremely low. Scaled theoretical: ~26 nW = 0.026 μW.

csf_harvesting.description: Theoretical scaled output from the same study
csf_harvesting.notes: Even theoretical scaling gives only 0.026 μW. CSF flow energy is fundamentally limited by low flow rate (0.3 mL/min) and low pressure differential (12 mmHg).

implant_power_requirements.description: Implantable wireless battery-free pressure sensing ASIC reported at 110.3 μW
implant_power_requirements.notes: This is a PUBLISHED implantable sensing ASIC power level. Sets the bar for what 'implantable sensing' requires.

implant_power_requirements.description: Our estimate: 10 μW pressure sensor + 20 μW flow sensor + 100 μW MCU (10% duty) + 500 μW RF (1% duty) = ~100 μW
implant_power_requirements.notes: This is our internal estimate. The 110.3 μW published ASIC (LITERATURE_VERIFIED) validates that ~100 μW is a reasonable order-of-magnitude for implantable sensing.

implant_power_requirements.description: Modern pacemakers consume ~5-25 μW average (very low duty cycle, ultra-low-power ASIC)
implant_power_requirements.notes: Pacemakers are the gold standard for ultra-low-power implantable devices. If they can run at 5-25 μW, P-15's target should be in this range, not 100 μW.

P15_power_architecture_tree.description: All power from cardiac motion harvesting. No external power. No battery.
P15_power_architecture_tree.sensor_duty_cycle: CONTINUOUS if sensor power < energy_in. Or INTERMITTENT if sensor power > energy_in.
P15_power_architecture_tree.controller_duty_cycle: INTERMITTENT — wake on sensor event, process, sleep
P15_power_architecture_tree.comms_duty_cycle: VERY LOW — accumulate data, transmit burst every hours/days

energy_out.note: If we target pacemaker-grade power budget (5-25 μW), not our original 100 μW estimate

P15_power_architecture_tree.verdict: MARGINAL — depends heavily on harvester design and power budget. Published pacemaker demos suggest FEASIBLE for ultra-low-power sensing. NOT feasible for our original 100 μW estimate. KEY INSIGHT: P-15's power budget should target pacemaker-grade (5-25 μW), not our inflated 100 μW.
P15_power_architecture_tree.p_tech_after_analysis: 0.15 (upgraded from 0.10 — published in-vivo demos show cardiac harvesting CAN power implantable devices, but at pacemaker-grade power budgets, not our original estimate)
P15_power_architecture_tree.condition: Requires ultra-low-power ASIC design (target <10 μW total). Requires optimized piezoelectric harvester (>10 μW in vivo). Both are published but not demonstrated together for SENSING (only for PACING).

P15_power_architecture_tree.architecture: B — Harvesting + Capacitor Buffer + Intermittent Operation
P15_power_architecture_tree.description: Harvest continuously into capacitor. Operate sensor/controller in bursts when capacitor has enough charge.
P15_power_architecture_tree.duty_cycle_calculation: If burst operation needs 100 μW for 1 second, and harvesting provides 1 μW, then need 100 seconds of harvesting per 1 second of operation. Duty cycle = 1%. Sensing burst every ~100 seconds.
P15_power_architecture_tree.energy_margin: FEASIBLE if duty cycle is acceptable. 1% duty cycle = sense every 100 seconds. For PRESSURE monitoring, 1 reading per 100 seconds may be clinically acceptable (ICP changes over minutes, not seconds).
P15_power_architecture_tree.verdict: FEASIBLE for intermittent sensing. Not feasible for continuous monitoring. Clinical acceptability of 1% duty cycle needs validation.
P15_power_architecture_tree.p_tech_after_analysis: 0.20 (more feasible than Architecture A because intermittent operation is less demanding)
P15_power_architecture_tree.condition: Requires clinical validation that intermittent sensing (1 reading per ~100 sec) is acceptable for the target application.

P15_power_architecture_tree.description: No active power. Passive sensor (e.g., LC resonant circuit whose resonance shifts with pressure). External reader interrogates wirelessly.
P15_power_architecture_tree.sensor_duty_cycle: CONTINUOUS (passive — always responsive to external interrogation)
P15_power_architecture_tree.comms_duty_cycle: ON DEMAND (external reader powers the communication)
P15_power_architecture_tree.verdict: FEASIBLE — this is how many existing passive implantable sensors work (e.g., passive LC pressure sensors). No energy harvesting needed. But: requires external reader device. Not truly 'self-powered.'
P15_power_architecture_tree.p_tech_after_analysis: 0.40 (passive sensing is well-established. But changes the product concept from 'self-powered' to 'passive + external reader')
P15_power_architecture_tree.condition: Changes P-15's value proposition. No longer 'self-powered' — becomes 'passive + external reader.' Buyer may prefer this if it eliminates battery AND harvesting complexity. But it's a different product.

P15_power_architecture_tree.description: Implant powered by external RF field (like NFC/RFID). No harvesting, no battery. External reader provides power wirelessly.

energy_in.value_uW: 100-1000 μW (from external RF reader at 10cm distance)

P15_power_architecture_tree.energy_storage: MINIMAL (small capacitor for brief operation after RF field removed)
P15_power_architecture_tree.energy_margin: FEASIBLE when reader is present. 0 when reader absent.
P15_power_architecture_tree.verdict: FEASIBLE but requires external reader. Same limitation as C. This is how some existing implantable sensors work (e.g., Codman MicroSensor is wired, but RF-powered versions exist in research).
P15_power_architecture_tree.p_tech_after_analysis: 0.35 (RF powering is established technology. But requires external reader, limiting to on-demand monitoring.)
P15_power_architecture_tree.condition: Same as C — changes product concept to 'externally powered.' Not truly 'self-powered.'

P15_power_architecture_tree.description: Cardiac harvesting for baseline sensing + RF boost for data transmission. Hybrid approach.
P15_power_architecture_tree.energy_storage: Capacitor (harvesting charges capacitor, RF provides burst power for transmission)
P15_power_architecture_tree.sensor_duty_cycle: CONTINUOUS (powered by harvesting at ultra-low power)
P15_power_architecture_tree.controller_duty_cycle: INTERMITTENT (wake on sensor event, powered by capacitor)
P15_power_architecture_tree.comms_duty_cycle: ON DEMAND (RF boost from external reader for data upload)
P15_power_architecture_tree.energy_margin: FEASIBLE — harvesting handles sensing, RF handles communication. Separates the two power-hungry functions.
P15_power_architecture_tree.verdict: MOST PROMISING — combines autonomous sensing (from harvesting) with on-demand communication (from RF). This is the architecture that published pacemaker demos effectively use (harvest for pacing, but data is read out separately).
P15_power_architecture_tree.p_tech_after_analysis: 0.30 (hybrid is more feasible than pure harvesting but adds RF reader dependency for communication)
P15_power_architecture_tree.condition: Requires: (1) ultra-low-power sensor (<1 μW continuous), (2) harvesting providing >1 μW average (LITERATURE_VERIFIED), (3) external reader for data upload. The sensor and harvester are the hard parts; the RF part is established.

P15_revised_verdict.overall: P-15 IS NOT DEAD. Architecture A (fully autonomous) is MARGINAL. Architecture B (intermittent) is FEASIBLE. Architecture C (passive) is FEASIBLE but changes the product. Architecture D (RF-powered) is FEASIBLE but requires external reader. Architecture E (hybrid) is MOST PROMISING.
P15_revised_verdict.key_insight: R297's 'INFEASIBLE' verdict was based on Architecture A with a 100 μW power budget. Published pacemaker-grade devices operate at 5-25 μW. At 5-25 μW, Architecture A becomes MARGINAL (not infeasible). Architecture B (intermittent) becomes FEASIBLE. Architecture E (hybrid) becomes MOST PROMISING.
P15_revised_verdict.p_tech_revised: 0.20 (upgraded from 0.10). Architecture A is marginal but not dead. Architectures B/C/D/E provide feasible paths. The concept is NOT killed — one architecture (A at 100 μW) failed, but the concept has alternatives.
P15_revised_verdict.tev_revised: 0.20 × 0.50 × $250K − $2K = $23,000 (upgraded from $10,500). P-15 moves up in ranking.
P15_revised_verdict.constitutional_principle_applied: Article XXIX: 'A failed embodiment cannot kill the invention unless the design space is exhausted.' Architecture A at 100 μW failed. Architectures B/C/D/E remain. Design space NOT exhausted.

P08_reformulation_attempt.question: Can P-08 become a passive/intermittently powered sensing or state-reporting system rather than a continuously powered active controller?

reformulation_analysis.passive_sensing: A passive CSF pressure sensor (LC resonant) would not need CSF energy harvesting. It would need external interrogation (same as P-15 Architecture C). This makes P-08 identical to P-15 Architecture C — the CSF energy source becomes irrelevant.
reformulation_analysis.intermittent_operation: At 0.026 μW theoretical scaled CSF harvesting, even intermittent operation requires 100,000 seconds of harvesting per 1 second of 100 μW operation. Duty cycle = 0.001%. One sensing burst every ~28 hours. NOT clinically useful.
reformulation_analysis.verdict: P-08's CSF energy harvesting is FUNDAMENTALLY limited by physics. CSF flow rate (0.3 mL/min) and pressure (12 mmHg) provide only 8 μW total hydraulic power. At any realistic harvester efficiency (<20%), this gives <2 μW. Even pacemaker-grade power budgets (5 μW) are not met. Passive sensing reformulation eliminates the need for CSF energy harvesting entirely, making P-08's specific mechanism (CSF energy harvesting) irrelevant.
reformulation_analysis.decision: P-08 ENTERS CEMETERY. The CSF energy harvesting mechanism is REFUTED by EXPERIMENTALLY_MEASURED data (0.62 nW, PubMed 28425028). The reformulation (passive sensing) eliminates the need for P-08's specific mechanism. P-08's concept (CSF-powered implant) is dead. The function (CSF sensing) can be served by P-15 Architecture C (passive + external reader) without P-08's CSF harvesting mechanism.

cemetary_entry.name: Energy-Neutral Micro-Assist (CSF Flow)
cemetary_entry.kill_reason: CSF flow energy harvesting REFUTED by EXPERIMENTALLY_MEASURED data (0.62 nW, PubMed 28425028). Total hydraulic power 8 μW. At realistic efficiency, <2 μW harvestable. Insufficient for any active implant function. Passive reformulation eliminates need for CSF harvesting mechanism.
cemetary_entry.constitutional_basis: Article XXIX: design space exhausted for CSF energy harvesting. The mechanism (not just one architecture) is infeasible.

bundle_vs_candidate_TEV.problem: R298 treated P-03 and P-07 as 'bundled' while still ranking them individually. This can distort portfolio value.
bundle_vs_candidate_TEV.solution: The canonical engine now distinguishes: (1) CANDIDATE_TEV — individual candidate's standalone value. (2) BUNDLE_TEV — value when purchased with parent. P-03's candidate TEV = $24K (standalone theoretical). P-03's bundle TEV = $0 (no standalone transaction; only purchased with P-01). Rankings show CANDIDATE_TEV but mark bundled candidates. Bundle value = parent TEV + bundled incremental. P-01 bundle (P-01+P-03) = $82K + $24K = $106K if buyer takes both.
bundle_vs_candidate_TEV.rule: Bundled candidates are shown in rankings with their STANDALONE TEV but marked BUNDLED. The optimizer does NOT add bundle TEV to parent TEV for ranking (avoids double-counting). Bundle value is reported separately.
